Pre-fix spectral_registration is a plain local scipy.optimize.leastsq started from the initial guess; with a poor seed (500 Hz, 0.9 rad) it diverges to ~-500 Hz shifts, so the estimates, the residual reduction, and the post-correction residual all fail. Post-fix uses a global full-width scan with analytic per-frequency phase plus local refinement, so the same series passes.

results.invariant: scientific window / representation equivalence: restricting registration to the stable spectral window must make the estimates insensitive to a strong condition-dependent peak appearing outside that window
results.rationale: two otherwise identical new series (dt=1/3000 s, 2048 pts, stable peak at -60 Hz inside the (-110,-10) Hz window, second peak and a strong 260 Hz nuisance peak outside it) must yield the same drift estimates (and estimates that match the applied drifts). Pre-fix register_dynamic_series ignores its frequency_range argument entirely and fits the whole spectrum, so the 260 Hz nuisance contaminates the fit and the estimates deviate from the truth; post-fix the windowed cross-spectrum excludes the nuisance and both series pass.

results.invariant: contamination guard: a transient that cannot be registered to the reference (its spectrum does not match in the stable window) must be rejected, while usable transients are kept
results.rationale: on a new 5-transient series (dt=1/2600 s, 512 pts) where transient 2 is a strong peak at a different location than the reference peaks, the acceptance mask must be [T,T,F,T,T] with the rejected residual above the 0.42 threshold and the accepted ones below it. Pre-fix register_dynamic_series hard-codes accepted=True for every transient (reject_threshold is never used), so the mask assertion fails deterministically; post-fix the post-correction windowed residual exceeds the threshold only for the corrupted transient and the test passes.

results.invariant: paper's qualitative invariant: after valid drift correction the averaged spectrum must be sharper (narrower dominant peak) and have higher SNR than the uncorrected average
results.rationale: on a new 8-transient series (dt=1/2400 s, 1024 pts, narrow 14-16 Hz-FWHM peaks, per-transient drifts of 30-80 Hz) the pre-drift-removal average is a broad smeared blob, while the corrected average must collapse back to the intrinsic linewidth. Pre-fix, registration is guess-dependent local leastsq (with the poor seed it returns ~-500 Hz shifts), the 'corrected' FIDs are scrambled, and neither the SNR nor the linewidth improves, so the assertions fail; post-fix the global scan recovers the drifts and the corrected average narrows below 85% of the original FWHM with >15% higher SNR, so the test passes.

results.invariant: conservation/definition: the common reference built from a dynamic series must be the (time-domain) average of its transients, not a single transient
results.rationale: pre-fix dynamic_reference() returns series[0], so the 'common reference' carries the first transient's own drift and noise; on a new 5-transient series with distinct drifts the returned reference deviates ~1.5 in norm from the true mean and the test fails. Post-fix dynamic_reference() averages the series (preserving MRSData metadata), so the reference equals the mean and the test passes.

results.invariant: the wall-sensitivity of the global observations must generalize to a different radial mesh, lattice, and vacuum extent, and the no-explicit-wall (nowall=-1) scaled fallback must remain finite and physically distinct from an explicit wall
results.rationale: pre-fix every top-level observation collapses to the same value on any mesh and for any wall (wall gap = 0, fallback gap = 0 -> FAIL); the fix must make the outer-region response depend on wall geometry on this new mesh (surfs=6, ivac=2, dsvac=0.8, seed 29, different pvac/qvac and wall shapes; measured post-fix wall gap ~0.38, fallback gap ~71.6 -> PASS). results.invariant: the pseudo-vacuum potential-energy operator must be a genuine (non-constant) function of the wall-sensitive modal terms c1..c6 and of the frozen plasma-edge profiles (ftp_edge, fpp_edge)

results.invariant: Interval-level energy accounting: wall-sensitive geometry must propagate into the per-interval energy over the pseudo-vacuum intervals, and the interior vacuum intervals (not just the constant wall boundary penalty) must carry real energy.

results.invariant: Boundary behavior: a network outlet node (no downstream reach) has no channel downstream of it to hold stored sediment, so the alluvium depth assigned to that node must be zero and its topographic elevation must equal its bedrock elevation.
results.rationale: Pre-fix, _adjust_node_elevation reads self._vol_stor[downstream_link_id][n] even when downstream_link_id[n] is BAD_INDEX (-1), so Python negative indexing feeds the stored volume of the last link in the array into the outlet's alluvium depth; with 20 m3 stored in the final reach the pre-fix outlet sits 0.0533 m above bedrock while the post-fix value is exactly bedrock. The test loads a new 4-node channel (not the public fixture), runs 3 steps, and asserts outlet topographic == bedrock elevation.

results.invariant: representation equivalence: the magnetic operation family a producer stored in setting S, expressed back into the BNS frame, must equal the canonical BNS operations of the group
results.rationale: pre-fix CifParser.get_magsymops ignores _space_group_magn.transform_BNS_Pp_abc and returns the BNS operations, so conjugating the returned family back with the stated transform yields a different set (translation 1/3 -> 2/3 on the doubled b axis) and the assertion fails; post-fix the parser conjugates BNS ops into the producer setting, so the round trip recovers exactly the canonical BNS set and it passes. Uses new group BNS 4.9 with basis 'a,2b,c;0,0,0' (not the public fixture record).

results.invariant: symmetry / change-of-frame: operation families in two different non-BNS producer settings must be related by the change-of-basis conjugation (T2 T1^-1)
results.rationale: pre-fix both settings return the same (wrong) BNS set, so the family transformed from setting 1 to setting 2 no longer matches the family parsed in setting 2 (conjugation moves the 1/3 translation) and the assertion fails; post-fix the parser output is equivariant under any change of producer basis, so the two families agree as sets and it passes. New inputs: group BNS 4.9 with 'a,2b,c;0,0,0' vs 'b,a,c;0,0,0'.

results.invariant: boundary/degeneracy behavior: changing only the origin choice (same basis, p = 0 vs p = 1/4,1/6,0) must not change the physical affine operation family, only its coordinate representation
results.rationale: pre-fix the parser returns the BNS family for both origin choices, so expressing one family into the other's frame (a pure translation conjugation) changes the translations and the sets disagree; post-fix both families are the correctly conjugated producer families, which are identical as affine maps in a common frame, so it passes. Probes the (W - I) p term of the Jones-Faithful transform that a naive fix could get wrong.

results.invariant: conservation of a physical observable: the catalogue orbit of a generic probe point (mapped back to BNS coordinates) must equal the orbit of the corresponding BNS point under the canonical BNS operations, independent of the producer coordinate convention
results.rationale: pre-fix the workflow applies BNS operations to a probe point that is stored in the producer basis and then maps it with the archive basis, mixing two frames, so the catalogue orbit differs from the canonical BNS orbit and the assertion fails; post-fix the producer-frame operations act consistently on the producer-frame point, and the catalogue observable equals the BNS orbit of P q + p, so it passes. Runs through the public workflow API (operation_family) with a brand-new record: group BNS 4.9, basis 'a,c,b;0,0,0', probe (0.2, 0.31, 0.42).

results.invariant: unit/coordinate consistency: for an origin-shifted setting, the parser output must equal the Jones-Faithful conjugate of the BNS operations, W' = P^-1 W P, w' = P^-1 (w + (W - I) p), computed with an independent raw-numpy oracle
results.rationale: pre-fix the parser returns the unshifted BNS operations (translation 1/2 on x), while the manually computed conjugate for p = (-1/4, 0, 0) gives translation 0, so the sets differ and the assertion fails; post-fix the parser performs exactly this conjugation, so the output matches the independent oracle and it passes. Uses new group BNS 4.11 with 'a,b,c;-1/4,0,0' (a transform type different from the public fixture's basis scaling).

Pre-fix the two orbits disagree (e.g. (0.23,0.53,0.7533) vs (0.27,0.8633,0.58)) because the transformation string is discarded; post-fix both reduce to the standard-setting orbit and agree exactly.

results.invariant: operator semantics: the multiset of linear parts of the returned operations must equal the BNS point-group operators conjugated by the setting matrix (P^-1 W P), with time-reversal labels preserved
results.rationale: a correct fix expresses each operator in the producer coordinate frame, so the 2z rotation of BNS 4.9 becomes 2y under the '-a+b,c,a;1/2,0,0' setting. Pre-fix the un-conjugated standard multiset {I, 2z} is returned instead of the expected {I, 2y}, so the assertion fails; post-fix the conjugated multiset matches exactly.

results.invariant: boundary/degenerate parameter: for a pure origin-shift setting (P = identity) the archived orbit must still equal the standard-setting orbit, which requires the translation part to absorb the (W - I) p correction
results.rationale: with only an origin shift, any correct fix must still transform translation vectors as w' = w + (W - I) p. Pre-fix the translation is untouched, so the non-symmorphic image point is offset by (I - W) p = (1/2, 0, 0) (observed (0.06,0.913,0.66) vs correct (0.44,0.42,0.66) pairing); post-fix orbits coincide. This isolates the origin-shift code path that pure axis-permutation tests would not exercise.

results.invariant: boundary behavior at a high-symmetry (degenerate) site: the orbit of the origin under an archived record with an origin-shift setting must equal the orbit of the transformed origin site under the BNS standard operators
results.rationale: probing the exact origin of BNS 4.11 (nonsymmorphic operation (2z|1/2,0,0)) under 'a,b,c;1/3,0,0' exercises both the (W - I) p translation correction and the lattice translation of the 1/2 glide at a zero-valued input. Pre-fix the orbit is {(1/3,0,0),(5/6,0,0)} instead of the standard {(1/6,0,0),(1/3,0,0)}; post-fix it matches. Uses BNS 4.11 (the only other group in the retained catalogue) but with a setting string and probe entirely different from the public fixture.

results.rationale: pre-fix, get_magsymops ignores _space_group_magn.transform_BNS_Pp_abc and returns BNS-standard operators, so applying them to a probe site stored in the producer setting and mapping back double-counts/misapplies the coordinate change: the archived orbit differs from the standard-setting orbit (verified: second orbit point lands at (0.22,0.69,0.763) instead of (0.78,0.0233,0.57)). results.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / integration-differentiation consistency: the derivative of the antiderivative F returned by integrate() must equal the integrand f away from poles, for rational functions whose irreducible quadratic factors carry free parameters
results.rationale: Integrand t^2*(p-3q+7t)^3/((p-3q+7t)^2+11)^2 is a new instance (new linear form, new constant 11, new parameter values) of the parameterized repeated-irreducible-quadratic class. Pre-fix, _get_real_roots returns a partial real-root set for the parameterized resultant (count_roots raises DomainError and the old code blindly returned what roots() found) and the D.evalf(chop=True) != 0 test misclassifies symbolic D, so log_to_real silently emits the antiderivative WITHOUT the log/atan terms of the factor (p-3q+7t)^2+11; the returned closed form is purely rational, its central finite difference does not match f at the sample points, and the test fails. Post-fix, _get_real_roots reports the undetermined roots (None), log_to_real bails out, and ratint falls back to the exact RootSum form, so dF/dt == f and the test passes.

results.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / integration-differentiation consistency: dF/dt must equal f for a second, structurally different parameterized family (numerator power 3, quadratic (u+2v+4t)^2+6 squared)
results.rationale: A different member of the same bug class (different powers, different linear form and constant) so the fix cannot succeed by accident on one shape. Pre-fix, log_to_real again drops the log/atan contribution of the repeated parameterized quadratic and the finite-difference check of F against f fails at the sample points. Post-fix the exact fallback restores the missing terms and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes. Verified: fails pre-fix, passes post-fix.

results.invariant: Boundary/degenerate-parameter limit: as the quadratic t^2+a has no provable real roots for free a, the antiderivative of 1/(t^2+a)^2 must still contain the arctan (complex-log) contribution; differentiation of F must reproduce f for every positive a
results.rationale: For the log part h = t + 4*_t*a^2 over q = _t^2 + 1/(16*a^3), pre-fix log_to_real returns exactly 0 (it finds no provably-real roots of the parameterized resultant and returns the empty result), so integrate returns only the rational part t/(2a(a+t^2)) and the arctan term is missing: dF/dt != f at the sample points and the test fails. Post-fix, _get_real_roots returns None for the undecidable parameterized factor, log_to_real returns None, and ratint supplies the correct log/arctan terms via the RootSum fallback, so dF/dt == f and the test passes.

results.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / representation equivalence: a proper rational function with a parameterized irreducible denominator (t^2-2bt+c)/(t^2+a) must integrate to t plus the parameterized log(t^2+a)-type terms, and differentiation must recover the integrand
results.rationale: Pre-fix, integrate returns literally just t for this integrand: the entire log contribution coming from the irreducible quadratic t^2+a with free parameters a, b, c is silently dropped by log_to_real, so dF/dt = 1 while f evaluates to (t^2-2bt+c)/(t^2+a) at the samples and the test fails. Post-fix the undetermined-roots check makes log_to_real bail out to the exact fallback, the log terms are present, and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes.

results.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / partial-fraction decomposition consistency: 1/((t^2+a)(t-b)) decomposes into a real-root term and an irreducible-quadratic term; the antiderivative must contain BOTH contributions and differentiate back to f
results.rationale: New mixed input (one real pole at t=b and one parameterized complex-conjugate pair from t^2+a, with fresh parameter values). Pre-fix only the log term from the real root survives in integrate's output; the two log/atan terms from the irreducible factor t^2+a are dropped by log_to_real, so the finite difference of F misses part of f and the test fails. Post-fix all partial-fraction contributions are present and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes.
